title: Rivers that run to one sea
hookLine: rivers run east and west, and all come from one sea
carry: we come from Being, and forget it
tomorrow: the son keeps saying 'teach me more.' why doesn't the father sigh?

lines: WHERE DO WE ALL COME FROM?
cards: Sunday dinner at a friend's house. Different food, a different grace before the meal, and somehow the same jokes about a cousin who's always late. It raises one question: where do all these different people come from?
Uddalaka answers with water. One river runs east. Another runs west.
They never meet on any map. But both end in the sea.

teach.h: FROM THE SEA, TO THE SEA.
teach.b: These rivers, my dear, the father says, the eastern ones flow east and the western ones flow west. From the sea they go to the sea.

teach.h: NO RIVER SAYS: I AM THIS ONE.
teach.b: They become the sea itself, and there they don't know, I am this river, I am that one. In the same way, he says, all these creatures, having come out of Being, don't know that they have come out of Being.
Whatever they are here, tiger or lion or gnat, that they become. The differences stay. What's missing is only the knowing.
Many Vedanta teachers call that not-knowing avidya: the work isn't to become one with Being, but to wake up to it. Then the refrain: that is the self; that you are.
A neighbor tradition has its own line about where people come from.

In the Christian Bible, in the book of Acts, the apostle Paul, speaking in Athens, says God "hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth." Here's what they share.
People who look and live very differently come from one source, and are more alike than they know. And the honest difference.

teach.h: MAKER AND MADE, OR ONE SELF.
teach.b: Paul speaks of God who made the nations: a maker, and the made. Uddalaka speaks of Being as the very self of each one, the river already made of sea. Two old answers to one question, each in its own words.

how: In Vedanta study, the rivers of Chandogya 6.10 are read right after the honey of 6.9. Acts 17:26 is part of the Christian New Testament, from Paul's speech in Athens.

o: that tribe is yours, so stay with your own
that you are: the same source in every life
that sea is far off, a place to reach later

games.q: the rivers, and a neighbor. tap the pairs.
p: flow east, and still reach the sea
where the rivers come from and return
maker and made, or one self

s: in the passage, the rivers start in the hills and only end in the sea
the father says: from the sea they go to the sea. they come from it as well as return to it.
in Acts, Paul says God made of one blood all nations
his words in Athens, in the King James Version: hath made of one blood all nations of men.

games.q: two cousins who grew up on opposite coasts meet and argue about whose side of the family is the 'real' one. what does the river picture point out?
o: both came from the same source; what's missing is only the knowing.
the river that runs east is the true one; the west is a copy.
rivers that split apart never share anything again.
games.why: eastern and western rivers both come from the sea and go back to it. creatures come from Being and don't know it; the father points at the knowing.

practice: Close your eyes and let each breath come in like a river and go out like one. Don't sort them, this breath, that breath; just let them arrive and leave. Rest on the father's words: from the sea they go to the sea.

wordCard.voice: Tat tvam asi: that you are. The rivers come from the sea, go back to the sea, and never knew they'd left it.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the sea. In the Chandogya, rivers go from the sea to the sea and become the sea itself.

carryVoice: Your line: we come from Being, and forget it. From the sea, to the sea. Until next time.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 6.10.1–3 (the eastern rivers flow east, the western west; from the sea they go to the sea and become the sea itself, and there do not know 'I am this one, I am that one'; so all creatures, having come from Being, do not know they have come from Being; whatever they are here, tiger, lion, wolf ... that they become; that which is the finest essence ... that you are, Shvetaketu; please, sir, teach me more)
